chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Miskan from Qutaybah al-A'sha who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him, saying to him: 'In the flock, the Jew and the Christian are sent; the exhibitor presents it and slaughters it. Can we eat his slaughter?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not include its price in your wealth, and do not eat it, for it is merely the Name (Bismillah), and one cannot be relied upon except a Muslim.'

The man said to him: 'Allah the Exalted says: This day the good things are made lawful for you, and the food of those who were given the Book is lawful for you.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to say: Rather, it is the grains and their like.'

key_terms.الاسْمُ: the Name (referring to the simple utterance of Bismillah)
key_terms.الْعَارِضَةُ: the exhibitor/presenter (who presents the animal for slaughter)
key_terms.طَعامُ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ: the food of those who were given the Book

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on eating meat slaughtered by Jews and Christians who say Bismillah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the general permissibility of the People of the Book's food and the specific requirement of reliable invocation (tasmiyah) for meat. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while the Quran permits their food, the invocation of Jews and Christians is often considered insufficiently reliable compared to a Muslim's, leading to the ruling of avoiding their meat. Furthermore, the Imam references his father, Imam al-Baqir, to interpret 'food' (ta'am) in verse 5:5 as referring to staple grains and fruits rather than slaughtered meat, a view supported by many Shia scholars to reconcile the verse with the practice of avoiding their meat.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar,f rom Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Ibn Muskan, from Quteyba Al A’asha who said,

‘A man asked Abu Abdullahasws and I was in hisasws presence, so he said to himasws, ‘The flock in which the Jews and the Christians are sent, so the exhibitors present therein, so he slaughters, can we eat his slaughter?’ So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Do not include its price in your wealth and do not eat it, for rather, it is the Naming (Bismillah), and none can be relied over it except for a Muslim’.

So the man said to himasws, ‘Allahazwj the High Says [5:5] This day (all) the good things are Permissible for you; and the food of those who have been Given the Book is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them’. So, Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘Myasws fatherasws was saying: ‘But rather, it is the grains and its like’.
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from ibn Muskan from Qutaybah al-A‘sha’ who has said the following:

“A man once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when I was with him (the Imam) and said, ‘Sheep are sent to Jews and Christian for maintenance and something happens and it is slaughtered; if I can use it for food. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Do not mix the price you receive for it with your other assets and do not use it for food. It is a matter of name (mentioning the name of Allah) and no one can be trusted in it except a Muslim.’

A man then said, ‘Allah, most High, says, ‘Today We have made the good things lawful for you and the food of the people of the book is lawful for you.’ [5:5] Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said to him, ‘My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say that it is about grains and similar things.’”
